Work modulo \(503\).  Since \(502=503-1\), reduce exponents modulo \(502\).

Let

\[
P(x)=(1+x)^{10000}.
\]

If we divide \(P(x)\) by \(x^{502}-1\), the remainder groups exponents by their residue modulo \(502\):

\[
P(x)=Q(x)(x^{502}-1)+\sum_{r=0}^{501} S_r x^r .
\]

So extracting the coefficient of \(x^r\) gives exactly \(S_r\) as an integer.

Now reduce modulo \(503\).  The multiplicative group \(\mathbb F_{503}^{\times}\) has order \(502\), so for any root \(\zeta\neq -1\) of \(x^{502}-1\),

\[
(1+\zeta)^{502}=1 \implies (1+\zeta)^{10000}=(1+\zeta)^{10000\bmod 502}.
\]

Since

\[
10000=19\cdot 502+462,
\]

we have

\[
(1+\zeta)^{10000}\equiv (1+\zeta)^{462}\pmod{503}.
\]

If \(\zeta=-1\), then both \((1+\zeta)^{10000}\) and \((1+\zeta)^{462}\) are \(0\).  Hence \((1+x)^{10000}-(1+x)^{462}\) vanishes at every \(502\)nd root of unity, so in \(\mathbb F_{503}[x]\),

\[
(1+x)^{10000}\equiv (1+x)^{462}\pmod{x^{502}-1}.
\]

Therefore the remainder satisfies

\[
\sum_{r=0}^{501} S_r x^r \equiv (1+x)^{462}
=\sum_{r=0}^{462}\binom{462}{r}x^r \pmod{503}.
\]

Thus

\[
S_r\equiv \binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}\qquad (0\le r\le 462),
\]

and

\[
S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}\qquad (463\le r\le 501).
\]

Because \(503\) is prime and \(503>462\), none of the binomial coefficients \(\binom{462}{r}\) for \(0\le r\le 462\) are divisible by \(503\).

Hence \(S_r\) is a multiple of \(503\) precisely for

\[
r=463,464,\dots,501.
\]

The number of such integers is

\[
501-463+1=39.
\]

\[
\boxed{39}
\]
